title: First words
goal: Greet people, say thank you and sorry the Hong Kong way, ask someone to repeat or slow down, and use numbers up to a thousand.

notes.h: Two ways to say thank you
notes.p: Use {{唔該|m4 goi1}} when someone does a small service for you: a waiter brings food, someone holds a door. It also means "please" when you ask for something. Use {{多謝|do1 ze6}} for a gift, a treat, a compliment or a birthday wish. When someone says {{唔該|m4 goi1}} to you, answer {{唔使唔該|m4 sai2 m4 goi1}} (no need to thank me).

{{唔好意思|m4 hou2 ji3 si1}} is light: excuse me, sorry to bother you, can I get past. {{對唔住|deoi3 m4 zyu6}} is a real apology: you stepped on someone's foot or broke something. If someone apologises to you and it's fine, say {{唔緊要|m4 gan2 jiu3}} (never mind).

There is no single word for yes. {{係|hai6}} means "it is" and {{唔係|m4 hai6}} "it isn't". For most questions you answer with the verb itself: asked {{你識唔識講廣東話呀？|nei5 sik1 m4 sik1 gong2 gwong2 dung1 waa2 aa3}} (do you speak Cantonese?), say {{識|sik1}} (yes, I can) or {{唔識|m4 sik1}} (no). Put {{唔|m4}}, a low hummed "m", before a verb to say "not". {{冇問題|mou5 man6 tai4}} (no problem) is a set phrase with a different "no" word, {{冇|mou5}} (there isn't).

Numbers build like arithmetic: {{三十八|saam1 sap6 baat3}} is three-ten-eight. Use {{零|ling4}} for an empty place in the middle: {{一百零五|jat1 baak3 ling4 ng5}} is 105. Careful: {{一百五|jat1 baak3 ng5}} with nothing after it means 150. Inside numbers, two is {{二|ji6}}: {{十二|sap6 ji6}}, {{二十|ji6 sap6}}. For two of something, use {{兩|loeng5}}: {{兩個人|loeng5 go3 jan4}}. Before hundred and thousand, people usually say {{兩|loeng5}} too: {{兩百|loeng5 baak3}}.

Tone changes the word. {{識|sik1}} (high, "know how to") and {{食|sik6}} (low, "eat") differ only in pitch. {{早晨|zou2 san4}} is good morning; {{早唞|zou2 tau2}} is good night. In {{廣東話|gwong2 dung1 waa2}} (Cantonese) the last syllable rises: waa2. {{五|ng5}} (five) is just a hummed "ng" with a small rise.
ex: ngo5 sik1 gong2 siu2 siu2 gwong2 dung1 waa2

vocab.note: Used with people you don't know well. Friends often skip it.
The everyday thank-you: a waiter brings food, someone holds a door. Also used to ask for something: 唔該，一杯茶 = a tea, please.

vocab.en: Thank you (for a gift or compliment)
vocab.note: For gifts, treats and compliments. For a small service, use 唔該.
晒 (saai3) adds "all / completely".
For bumping into someone, interrupting, or a small apology.
Cantonese has no single word for "yes". 係 means "it is"; often you answer by repeating the verb.
唔 (m4) = not.
From English "bye-bye". The most common goodbye in Hong Kong.
啲 (di1) after a describing word = "a bit more".

t: ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 gong2 do1 ci3 aa3
vocab.en: Can you say it one more time?
vocab.note: Questions are often "can-not-can": 可唔可以 = can or can't.

t: ngo5 sik1 gong2 siu2 siu2 gwong2 dung1 waa2
vocab.note: 話 is said waa2 here, not its dictionary tone waa6.
Use 二 when counting and inside numbers (12, 20). Use 兩 for "two of something".
兩個人 = two people.
Only the "ng" sound, no vowel: hum "ng" with a small rise.
Numbers build like arithmetic: ten-one = 11.
two-ten = 20.
{{明|ming4}} = understand. Add {{唔|m4}} for the opposite.
{{知|zi1}} = know (a fact).
Literally "no need to thank". The reply when someone says {{唔該|m4 goi1}} to you.

t: nei5 sik1 m4 sik1 gong2 gwong2 dung1 waa2 aa3
vocab.note: Answer with the verb: {{識|sik1}} (yes) or {{唔識|m4 sik1}} (no).
Said before bed or when parting late at night. Don't mix it up with {{早晨|zou2 san4}}.
Inside a number, two is always {{二|ji6}}.
{{零|ling4}} fills the empty tens place. {{一百五|jat1 baak3 ng5}} alone means 150.
{{兩|loeng5}} is the usual word before hundred and thousand.
{{個|go3}} is a counting word that goes between the number and the noun. Before it, two is always {{兩|loeng5}}.

items.why: {{知|zi1}} = know. {{我唔明|ngo5 m4 ming4}} would be "I don't understand".
{{對唔住|deoi3 m4 zyu6}} is a real apology.
{{千|cin1}} = thousand, {{百|baak3}} = hundred.
{{唔好意思|m4 hou2 ji3 si1}} is the light "excuse me / sorry".

q: ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 gong2 ___ ci3 aa3
items.en: Can you say it one more time?
items.why: {{講多次|gong2 do1 ci3}} = say it one more time.
{{啲|di1}} after a describing word means "a bit more": {{慢啲|maan6 di1}} = a bit slower.
{{晒|saai3}} adds "all, completely": {{唔該晒|m4 goi1 saai3}} = thanks a lot.

q: ho2 ___ ho2 ji5 gong2 do1 ci3 aa3
items.en: Can you say it one more time?
items.why: "Can-not-can": {{可唔可以|ho2 m4 ho2 ji5}}. {{唔|m4}} is the "not" that goes before verbs.
Someone thanked you with {{唔該|m4 goi1}}; you answer "no need to {{唔該|m4 goi1}}": {{唔使唔該|m4 sai2 m4 goi1}}.
Inside a number, two is {{二|ji6}}: {{二十|ji6 sap6}}.
{{唔|m4}} goes before a verb to make it "not": {{我唔明|ngo5 m4 ming4}}.
Inside a number, two is always {{二|ji6}}: {{十二|sap6 ji6}}. {{兩|loeng5}} is for two of something.
Two of something is {{兩|loeng5}}: {{兩個人|loeng5 go3 jan4}}. {{二個人|ji6 go3 jan4}} is wrong.
{{零|ling4}} fills the empty tens place. Without it, {{一百五|jat1 baak3 ng5}} means 150.

q: ngo5 ___ gong2 siu2 siu2 gwong2 dung1 waa2
items.why: {{識|sik1}} (high tone) = know how to. {{食|sik6}} (low tone) = eat.
{{冇|mou5}} = there isn't. {{唔|m4}} goes before verbs, not in this phrase. {{好問題|hou2 man6 tai4}} would mean "good question".

items.q: The waiter puts your food on the table. You say:
items.why: A small service gets {{唔該|m4 goi1}}. {{唔使唔該|m4 sai2 m4 goi1}} is what the waiter would say back.

items.q: A friend gives you a birthday present. You say:
items.why: For a gift, {{多謝|do1 ze6}}. {{唔該|m4 goi1}} is for a service.

items.q: You held the door and the man says {{唔該|m4 goi1}} to you. You reply:
items.why: {{唔使唔該|m4 sai2 m4 goi1}} = no need to thank me.

items.q: Someone is standing in the lift doorway and you need to get past. You say:
items.why: {{唔好意思|m4 hou2 ji3 si1}} is the light "excuse me".

items.q: The shopkeeper is talking fast. You want her to slow down. You say:
opts: ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 gong2 do1 ci3 aa3
items.why: {{慢啲|maan6 di1}} = slower. {{講多次|gong2 do1 ci3}} asks her to repeat, not to slow down.

items.q: It's eight in the morning and you meet your neighbour in the lift. You say:
items.why: {{早晨|zou2 san4}} = good morning. {{早唞|zou2 tau2}} = good night.

items.q: Someone bumps into you and says {{對唔住|deoi3 m4 zyu6}}. You're fine. You say:
items.why: {{唔緊要|m4 gan2 jiu3}} = never mind, it's fine.

items.q: Someone asks {{你識唔識講廣東話呀？|nei5 sik1 m4 sik1 gong2 gwong2 dung1 waa2 aa3}} You can speak a little. You answer:
items.why: Answer with the verb: {{識|sik1}} = yes, I can. {{食|sik6}} (low tone) means eat.

items.en: Can you say it one more time?
full: ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 gong2 do1 ci3 aa3
ngo5 sik1 gong2 siu2 siu2 gwong2 dung1 waa2
deoi3 m4 zyu6, ngo5 m4 ming4

items.en: Can you speak a bit slower?
full: ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 gong2 maan6 di1 aa3

items.why: {{唔|m4}} = not; {{明|ming4}} = understand; {{知|zi1}} would be know.

say: ngo5 sik1 gong2 siu2 siu2 gwong2 dung1 waa2
opts: I speak a lot of Cantonese.
items.why: {{識講|sik1 gong2}} = can speak; {{少少|siu2 siu2}} = a little.
two-ten-five = 25.
nine-ten-nine = 99.
{{零|ling4}} means the tens place is empty: 302. {{三百二|saam1 baak3 ji6}} would be 320.

opts: Please say it one more time.
items.why: {{慢啲|maan6 di1}} = a bit slower.
With {{零|ling4}} it is 108. {{一百八|jat1 baak3 baat3}} without it would be 180.
{{唔使|m4 sai2}} = no need: no need to thank me.
{{早唞|zou2 tau2}} = good night; {{早晨|zou2 san4}} = good morning.

say: deoi3 m4 zyu6, ngo5 m4 zi1
items.why: {{對唔住|deoi3 m4 zyu6}} = sorry; {{唔知|m4 zi1}} = don't know.

turns.why: Answer with {{早晨|zou2 san4}}. {{早唞|zou2 tau2}} is good night.

s: nei5 sik1 gong2 gwong2 dung1 waa2 gaa3

turns.why: She's leaving, so {{拜拜|baai1 baai3}}. She hasn't done anything to thank her for.

opts: ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 gong2 do1 ci3 aa3
turns.why: You didn't catch it, so ask her to say it one more time.
She helped you, so thank her with {{唔該晒|m4 goi1 saai3}}. {{唔使唔該|m4 sai2 m4 goi1}} is the reply to thanks.
Two of something is {{兩|loeng5}}, never {{二|ji6}}. And he guessed right, so {{係呀|hai6 aa3}}.
A small service gets {{唔該|m4 goi1}}.

s: 你好！你識唔識講廣東話呀？
nei5 hou2! nei5 sik1 m4 sik1 gong2 gwong2 dung1 waa2 aa3

turns.why: Answer with the verb: {{識|sik1}} = yes, I can. {{唔識|m4 sik1}} and "a little" contradict each other.

s: 好呀，咁我哋講廣東話啦！
hou2 aa3, gam2 ngo5 dei6 gong2 gwong2 dung1 waa2 laa1
turns.en: (very fast) Great, then let's speak Cantonese!

turns.why: He spoke too fast, so ask him to slow down.
For a present or a wish, {{多謝|do1 ze6}}.
Good night back: {{早唞|zou2 tau2}}. {{早晨|zou2 san4}} is good morning.

roleplay.title: Morning in the building
roleplay.setup: You meet a friendly older neighbour in the lift of your Hong Kong building. Greet her, thank her when she holds the door, and say goodbye.
roleplay.persona: You are Auntie Wong, a friendly retired woman in Hong Kong. Speak simple colloquial Hong Kong Cantonese using only level 1 words: greetings (早晨, 你好, 拜拜), 唔該 / 多謝, 唔好意思 / 對唔住, 係 / 唔係, 識 / 唔識, and numbers. Use very short sentences. Say good morning, hold the lift door so the learner can say 唔該, and ask whether they speak Cantonese (你識唔識講廣東話呀？). If they ask you to repeat or slow down, do it. Never use English.
goals: Say you speak a little Cantonese
Thank her when she holds the door

roleplay.title: Numbers at the counter
roleplay.setup: You're at a counter in a Hong Kong post office. The clerk calls ticket numbers and reads out numbers quickly. Ask her to repeat or slow down, say the numbers back, and thank her.
roleplay.persona: You are Miss Lee, a busy but kind post office clerk in Hong Kong. Speak simple colloquial Hong Kong Cantonese using only level 1 words: numbers from zero to a thousand, 係 / 唔係, 唔該, 唔使唔該. Read out numbers quickly at first (for example 一百零八, 三百二十五, 六百零七). If the learner asks you to repeat (可唔可以講多次呀？) or slow down (唔該講慢啲), do it. When they say a number back, confirm with 係 or correct them with 唔係 and the right number.
goals: Ask her to say a number again
